title: How to Keep Anger from Getting the Best of You with Howard Kassinove, PhD, and Raymond “Chip” Tafrate, PhD

sentences.en: We all know what it feels like to get angry.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道生气是什么感觉。

sentences.en: Another driver cuts you off in traffic or runs a red light right in front of you.
sentences.zh: 另一个司机在交通拥堵时强行超车，或者在你面前闯红灯。

sentences.en: You miss out on a promotion to someone you feel is less deserving.
sentences.zh: 你错过了一次升职机会，而你觉得那个得到机会的人根本不配。

sentences.en: Your kid stomps away yelling that they won't listen to you anymore.
sentences.zh: 你的孩子气冲冲地走开，大喊着说再也不听你的话了。

sentences.en: Your stomach churns, your pulse races, and you think, how dare they?
sentences.zh: 你胃里翻江倒海，脉搏加速，心里想：他们怎么敢这样？

sentences.en: Anger is a normal human emotion.
sentences.zh: 愤怒是一种正常的人类情绪。

sentences.en: A natural reaction when you feel that something or someone has done you wrong.
sentences.zh: 当你觉得某事或某人对你做了错事时的一种自然反应。

sentences.en: But anger can also turn violent and dangerous.
sentences.zh: 但愤怒也可能变得暴力和危险。

sentences.en: It can ruin relationships and it can interfere with our health and our happiness.
sentences.zh: 它会毁掉人际关系，还会干扰我们的健康和幸福。

sentences.en: So how do you know when anger is healthy and when it's harmful?
sentences.zh: 那么，你怎么知道什么时候的愤怒是健康的，什么时候又是具有破坏性的呢？

sentences.en: Are there effective strategies you can use to cope with anger when it's interfering with your life?
sentences.zh: 当愤怒干扰了你的生活时，有没有什么有效的策略可以用来应对？

sentences.en: What if your anger threshold is different from that of your partner?
sentences.zh: 如果你的愤怒阈值和伴侣的不同，该怎么办？

sentences.en: When you feel angry, is it better to let it all out or hold your emotions in?
sentences.zh: 当你感到愤怒时，是把情绪全部宣泄出来更好，还是压抑在心里更好？

sentences.en: And how do you know if it's time to seek help from a psychologist or other mental health professional?
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道什么时候该向心理学家或其他心理健康专业人士寻求帮助？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学说话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: We have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 我们今天有两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: First is Dr. Howard Kasanoff, a professor emeritus of psychology at Hofstra University,
sentences.zh: 第一位是霍华德·卡萨诺夫博士，霍夫斯特拉大学心理学荣休教授，

sentences.en: where he was the founder and director of the Institute for the Study and Treatment of Anger and Aggression.
sentences.zh: 他曾在那里创立并领导了愤怒与攻击行为研究与治疗研究所。

sentences.en: Dr. Kasanoff has more than 40 years of experience as a scientist and a clinical practitioner studying anger and aggression management.
sentences.zh: 卡萨诺夫博士作为一名科学家和临床从业者，拥有40多年研究和管理愤怒与攻击行为的经验。

sentences.en: Our second guest is Dr. Raymond Chip Tafrady, a clinical psychologist and professor in the Department of Criminology and Criminal Justice at Central Connecticut State University.
sentences.zh: 我们的第二位嘉宾是雷蒙德·奇普·塔夫拉迪博士，他是中康涅狄格州立大学犯罪学与刑事司法系的临床心理学家兼教授。

sentences.en: Dr. Tafrady frequently consults with criminal justice agencies and programs, community mental health centers, and private practices,
sentences.zh: 塔夫拉迪博士经常为刑事司法机构和项目、社区心理健康中心以及私人诊所提供咨询，

sentences.en: and has trained thousands of professionals to work more effectively with adolescents and adults with difficult-to-change anger probleMs.
sentences.zh: 并培训了数千名专业人员，以便更有效地帮助那些有难以改变的愤怒问题的青少年和成年人。

sentences.en: Together, Dr. Kasanoff and Dr. Tafrady have authored two books,
sentences.zh: 卡萨诺夫博士和塔夫拉迪博士合著了两本书，

sentences.en: Anger Management for Everyone, Ten Proven Strategies to Help You Control Anger and Live a Happier Life, and The Practitioner's Guide to Anger Management.
sentences.zh: 《人人适用的愤怒管理：帮助你控制愤怒、过上更幸福生活的十个经验证实的策略》以及《从业者愤怒管理指南》。

sentences.en: Thank you both for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢两位今天参加我的节目。

sentences.en: Our pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的荣幸。

sentences.en: Great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Let's start with what we mean by anger.
sentences.zh: 让我们从我们所说的愤怒的含义开始讨论。

sentences.en: People often think that anger and aggression are synonymous, but they're not the same thing.
sentences.zh: 人们经常认为愤怒和攻击性是同义词，但它们并不是同一回事。

sentences.en: So what is anger?
sentences.zh: 那么，什么是愤怒？

sentences.en: How is it different from aggression?
sentences.zh: 它与攻击性有什么不同？

sentences.en: And Dr. Kasanoff, let's start with you on that one.
sentences.zh: 卡萨诺夫博士，我们先从您开始探讨这个问题。

sentences.en: You know, anger is a complex reaction to perceived threat.
sentences.zh: 你知道，愤怒是对感知到的威胁的一种复杂反应。

sentences.en: We can feel threatened when our children are hurt by other kids.
sentences.zh: 当我们的孩子被其他孩子欺负时，我们会感到受到威胁。

sentences.en: We can feel threatened in the workplace.
sentences.zh: 我们在职场中可能会感到受到威胁。

sentences.en: We can feel threatened by neighbors.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会受到来自邻居的威胁。

sentences.en: There are all kinds of threats that exist in our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们的生活中存在着各种各样的威胁。

sentences.en: And anger emerges when we perceive that threat.
sentences.zh: 当我们感知到这种威胁时，愤怒就会产生。

sentences.en: And when I say it's complex, what I mean is that when we become angry, we often have thoughts that go through our mind, like the boss has given the raise to another worker.
sentences.zh: 当我说它很复杂时，我的意思是，当我们生气时，我们的脑海中往往会闪过各种想法，比如老板把加薪给了一个别的员工。

sentences.en: He shouldn't have done that.
sentences.zh: 他不该那样做。

sentences.en: This is a terrible, awful thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件糟糕透顶的事情。

sentences.en: So we have these thoughts that go through our mind.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的脑海中会闪过这些想法。

sentences.en: We also have a lot of behaviors.
sentences.zh: 我们也会有大量的行为表现。

sentences.en: And by that, I mean we will yell and scream and flail our hands around.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们会大喊大叫、挥舞双手。

sentences.en: We may engage in some kind of vengeance against the other person.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会对另一个人实施某种报复。

sentences.en: And, of course, there are physiological or biological reactions also to threat, where our heart rate increases and our response to light increases, and we secrete chemicals.
sentences.zh: 当然，对于威胁，也会有生理或生物学上的反应，比如我们的心率加快，对光的反应增加，还会分泌化学物质。

sentences.en: And so it's this complex reaction, all of which has to be dealt with in therapy or in treatment.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种复杂的反应，所有这些都需要在治疗或干预中得到处理。

sentences.en: The second part, what's the difference between anger and aggression, is very interesting.
sentences.zh: 第二部分，愤怒和攻击性的区别是什么，这非常有趣。

sentences.en: Anger is primarily an internal response.
sentences.zh: 愤怒主要是一种内在反应。

sentences.en: As a matter of fact, if you look in terms of international or national negotiations, if a person becomes angry, you're not supposed to let your opponent know about it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你从国际或国家谈判的角度来看，如果一个人生气了，你是不能让你的对手知道这一点的。

sentences.en: On the other hand, most people who become angry do not become aggressive.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，大多数生气的人并不会变得具有攻击性。

sentences.en: We just become angry.
sentences.zh: 我们只是生气。

sentences.en: We let it seethe inside of us.
sentences.zh: 我们让它在内心暗自翻涌。

sentences.en: Maybe we talk to our marital partner about it, etc.
sentences.zh: 也许我们会跟我们的配偶谈论这件事，等等。

sentences.en: Aggression, on the other hand, can definitely occur without any anger at all.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，攻击性完全可以在没有任何愤怒的情况下发生。

sentences.en: Think for a moment about a hunter going out for the day to shoot animals.
sentences.zh: 试想一下一个猎人出门一天去射杀动物的情形。

sentences.en: That hunter is not angry at the animals.
sentences.zh: 那个猎人对动物并没有生气。

sentences.en: He or she sees it as an activity of the day.
sentences.zh: 他或她将这视为当天的日常活动。

sentences.en: So anger can be followed by aggression, but most of the time it's not.
sentences.zh: 因此，愤怒之后可能会伴随攻击性，但大多数时候并非如此。

sentences.en: Aggression can occur after anger.
sentences.zh: 攻击性可能发生在愤怒之后。

sentences.en: As I said, most of the time it's not.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，大多数时候并非如此。

sentences.en: But aggression can be a totally independent behavior where the goal is to harm, to engage in some kind of behavioral harm without any anger at all.
sentences.zh: 但攻击性可以是一种完全独立的行为，其目标是伤害，即在没有任何愤怒的情况下实施某种行为上的伤害。

sentences.en: Chip, did you want to say something?
sentences.zh: 奇普，你想说点什么吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think this is a common misunderstanding about anger.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是人们对愤怒的一个普遍误解。

sentences.en: People think of the word anger and the next word that pops into their mind is aggression.
sentences.zh: 人们一想到“愤怒”这个词，脑海中蹦出的下一个词就是“攻击性”。

sentences.en: And in a lot of anger training workshops, we sometimes do this exercise.
sentences.zh: 在许多愤怒培训工作坊中，我们有时会做这样一个练习。

sentences.en: We ask all the participants, and they're usually practitioners of different types.
sentences.zh: 我们询问所有参与者，他们通常是不同类型的从业人员。

sentences.en: We ask them, how many of you have experienced anger in the past week?
sentences.zh: 我们问他们：你们中有多少人在过去一周里体验过愤怒？

sentences.en: And it's normal for people to feel angry, you know, one or two times a week.
sentences.zh: 人们感到生气是很正常的，你知道的，一周一两次。

sentences.en: That's just typical.
sentences.zh: 这很典型。

sentences.en: And so when you ask a room full of people to let you know if they've experienced anger, pretty much all the hands in the room go up.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你询问满屋子的人让他们表明自己是否体验过愤怒时，房间里几乎所有的手都举了起来。

sentences.en: And then you ask a second question.
sentences.zh: 然后你问第二个问题。

sentences.en: How many of you have assaulted somebody, destroyed property, punched a wall, kicked somebody in the past week when you were angry,
sentences.zh: 你们中有多少人在过去一周生气时殴打过某人、破坏过财产、捶过墙、踢过某人，

sentences.en: and there's almost no hands that go up in the room?
sentences.zh: 房间里几乎没有人举手。

sentences.en: But the most interesting question is the next one.
sentences.zh: 但最有趣的问题是下一个。

sentences.en: How many of you at some point in your life when you were angry have hit, struck, pushed, kicked somebody?
sentences.zh: 你们中有多少人在一生的某个时候生气时打过、袭击过、推过、踢过某人？

sentences.en: And it's an uncomfortable moment, but almost all the hands in the room go up again.
sentences.zh: 这是一个令人尴尬的时刻，但房间里几乎所有的手又都举起来了。

sentences.en: And so I think what Howie and I are saying is that aggression is the least common response often when people are angry.
sentences.zh: 所以我想霍威和我所表达的意思是，当人们生气时，攻击性往往是最不常见的反应。

sentences.en: And on studies where they actually count and measure this, anger is the thing that happens kind of, it's like the least common thing on most of these surveys.
sentences.zh: 在那些真正对此进行统计和测量的研究中，愤怒发生的情况，可以说是这些调查中最少见的一种。

sentences.en: However, as the hands in the room exercise shows, that all of us know the connection between anger and aggression.
sentences.zh: 然而，正如房间里举手的练习所显示的那样，我们所有人都知道愤怒和攻击性之间的联系。

sentences.en: Most of us have been there, and we understand the destructive connection that can occur.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人都经历过，并且我们理解可能发生的这种破坏性联系。

sentences.en: And I would say for most of the listeners on this podcast, probably some of your most cringeworthy moments occurred when you were angry at somebody.
sentences.zh: 我想对于这个播客的大多数听众来说，你最感到尴尬的时刻可能有一些就发生在当你对某人生气的时候。

sentences.en: So to follow up on that, is there a, quote, normal level of anger, a normal amount of anger that people could expect to experience during a week, during a month, during a lifetime?
sentences.zh: 那么顺着这个话题，是否存在一个所谓的“正常水平的愤怒”，即人们在一周内、一个月内、一生中可以预料到会体验到的正常愤怒量？

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, Chip gives the notion of once or twice a week is kind of normal.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道的，奇普提到的“一周一两次”可以说是正常的。

sentences.en: We use four criteria.
sentences.zh: 我们使用四个标准来衡量。

sentences.en: We ask, is the anger that you're experiencing too frequent, too intense?
sentences.zh: 我们问：你体验到的愤怒是不是太频繁了、太强烈了？

sentences.en: Does it endure for too long?
sentences.zh: 它持续的时间是不是太长了？

sentences.en: And is your anger helpful?
sentences.zh: 你的愤怒是有益的吗？

sentences.en: Is it working in your family, in your job?
sentences.zh: 它在你的家庭、工作中起作用吗？

sentences.en: Is it making you a more productive citizen?
sentences.zh: 它有没有让你成为一个更有成效的公民？

sentences.en: So if you're becoming angry once a week, twice a week, if it's of low level, if it doesn't endure, and by that I mean you don't let the anger fester for days and weeks and months,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你每周生气一次、两次，如果它的程度很低，如果它没有持续很久——我的意思是，你没有让愤怒在几天、几周和几个月里不断发酵，

sentences.en: and if your anger is serving as a signal, I would say, in other words, let's take that workplace example again.
sentences.zh: 并且如果你的愤怒起到了一种信号的作用，换句话说，让我们再次以那个职场例子为例。

sentences.en: The boss hires somebody and that other person is getting some extra benefits, and you're aware of this, and you kind of become a little bit agitated, a little bit.
sentences.zh: 老板雇用了某人，而那个人得到了额外的好处，你注意到了这一点，你开始感到有点烦躁，有一点点。

sentences.en: Then the anger is serving as a useful signal to talk to the boss and say, you know, I've been here for a long time,
sentences.zh: 然后，愤怒作为一个有用的信号提醒你去跟老板谈谈，并说：“你知道的，我已经在这里工作很长时间了，

sentences.en: and this new guy or new woman has a better desk or has better working hours or things like that, and I'd like to talk to you about that.
sentences.zh: 而这个新来的员工（无论男女）有更好的办公桌、更好的工作时间或诸如此类的事情，我想跟你谈谈这件事。”

sentences.en: So, yes, not too intense, not too enduring, not too frequent, and helpful.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，不过分强烈、不过分持久、不过分频繁且有益。

sentences.en: That's the sign of good anger.
sentences.zh: 这就是良好愤怒的标志。

sentences.en: So, then, is there a clinical anger disorder, and if so, what are the hallmarks?
sentences.zh: 那么，是否存在临床上的愤怒障碍？如果有的话，它的主要特征是什么？

sentences.en: Well, you know, Chip and I, and Chip, we can both answer this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，奇普和我，奇普，我们两个都可以回答这个问题。

sentences.en: Regrettably, there is not an official diagnosis that's a clinical anger disorder.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，并没有一个被官方承认的诊断叫做“临床愤怒障碍”。

sentences.en: And I would say, you know, think about this.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以这样想：

sentences.en: Human beings were brought up as part of the fight or flight reaction.
sentences.zh: 人类是作为“战斗或逃跑”反应的一部分进化而来的。

sentences.en: So, anger is an approach emotion, and it occurs when you feel threatened.
sentences.zh: 所以，愤怒是一种“趋近”情绪，当你感到受到威胁时它就会产生。

sentences.en: Anxiety is a withdrawal emotion, and if you feel threatened, you withdraw.
sentences.zh: 焦虑是一种“回避”情绪，如果你感到受到威胁，你就会退缩。

sentences.en: We have lots of anxiety diagnoses, but we've had no anger diagnoses.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多关于焦虑的诊断，但我们却没有关于愤怒的诊断。

sentences.en: And when we try to bring this up to our colleagues, we don't make much headway at all.
sentences.zh: 当我们试图向我们的同事提出这一点时，我们根本没有取得什么实质性进展。

sentences.en: Why do you think they're resistant to that?
sentences.zh: 你认为他们为什么对此产生抗拒？

sentences.en: I think because anger is considered to be a moral emotion.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为愤怒被认为是一种道德情绪。

sentences.en: And by that, I mean, oh, you're suffering from anxiety.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，哦，你正在遭受焦虑的折磨。

sentences.en: Oh, you poor person.
sentences.zh: 哦，你这个可怜的人。

sentences.en: I feel so sad for you.
sentences.zh: 我为你感到很难过。

sentences.en: I feel so bad for you.
sentences.zh: 我为你感到非常糟糕。

sentences.en: And we'd better have all these diagnoses and treatments to help you.
sentences.zh: 我们最好有所有这些诊断和治疗来帮助你。

sentences.en: Anger, on the other hand, is you shouldn't have done it.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，对于愤怒，我们的态度则是：你本不该那样做。

sentences.en: You're an evil person.
sentences.zh: 你是个邪恶的人。

sentences.en: I want to punish you.
sentences.zh: 我要惩罚你。

sentences.en: And that doesn't lead to diagnoses.
sentences.zh: 这不会带来诊断。

sentences.en: That leads to criminal justice intervention.
sentences.zh: 这会带来刑事司法干预。

sentences.en: Chip, did you want to?
sentences.zh: 奇普，你想说点什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think there's a lot of reasons why anger has been ignored historically.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为愤怒在历史上被忽视有很多原因。

sentences.en: And you have to kind of almost go back to the Western philosophers who got it right, who really labeled anger as a sort of significant human problem.
sentences.zh: 你几乎不得不回溯到那些看清了这一点的西方哲学家，他们真正将愤怒贴上了某种重大人类的标签。

sentences.en: And then along came psychology, and anger and aggression became sort of intertwined in psychoanalytic theory, the idea that everyone has sort of an innate aggressive drive.
sentences.zh: 然后心理学兴起了，愤怒和攻击性在精神分析理论中被交织在了一起，这种观点认为每个人都有一种与生俱来的攻击驱动力。

sentences.en: And the behaviorists also kind of lumped anger and aggression together, the idea that anger is just sort of a weaker expression of aggression.
sentences.zh: 行为主义者也将愤怒和攻击性混为一谈，认为愤怒只是攻击性的较弱表现形式。

sentences.en: And then we get to another area where they've got it right, emotion researchers.
sentences.zh: 然后我们来到了另一个看清了这一点的领域——情绪研究人员。

sentences.en: Emotion researchers have suggested that there's a handful of basic emotions that all human beings are capable of experiencing.
sentences.zh: 情绪研究人员指出，有一小部分基本情绪是所有人类都能够体验到的。

sentences.en: They're interwoven into the fabric of our sort of evolution.
sentences.zh: 它们交织在我们进化的结构中。

sentences.en: And anger is one of those basic emotions.
sentences.zh: 愤怒就是其中一种基本情绪。

sentences.en: It's on everybody's liSt.
sentences.zh: 它在每个人的清单上。

sentences.en: And so, I think that that's one of the reasons why anger has been ignored.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这是愤怒被忽视的原因之一。

sentences.en: It's just the sort of historical place that anger has had in psychology.
sentences.zh: 这只是愤怒在心理学中一直以来的历史地位所致。

sentences.en: And sometimes we refer to anger as the forgotten emotion because there's no diagnostic category where the emotional excess is primarily anger.
sentences.zh: 有时我们将愤怒称为“被遗忘的情绪”，因为没有任何一个诊断分类将情绪过剩主要归咎于愤怒。

sentences.en: And in fact, anger is rarely mentioned in the DSM.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》（DSM）中很少提及愤怒。

sentences.en: It's always a secondary symptom to other probleMs.
sentences.zh: 它总是作为其他问题的次要症状出现。

sentences.en: And there's another, I think, more practical reason that as psychologists, when we pick our areas of study, we spent our lives studying anxiety and depression.
sentences.zh: 我认为还有一个更实际的原因，那就是作为心理学家，当我们选择研究领域时，我们毕生都在研究焦虑和抑郁。

sentences.en: And maybe it's because anxious and depressive individuals are a little easier to work with.
sentences.zh: 也许是因为焦虑和抑郁的个体稍微更容易相处。

sentences.en: Angry clients can be difficult.
sentences.zh: 暴躁的来访者可能会很难应对。

sentences.en: They can be unpredictable, unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 他们可能喜怒无常、令人不快。

sentences.en: And I think in some ways, professionals have not embraced people with anger probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我认为在某些方面，专业人士并没有真正接纳有愤怒问题的人。

sentences.en: So, let me ask if there is a significant gender difference in how people tend to experience and express anger.
sentences.zh: 那么，请允许我问一下，在人们体验和表达愤怒的方式上，是否存在显著的性别差异？

sentences.en: Do women or men get angry more often or do they just express anger differently?
sentences.zh: 是女性还是男性更容易生气，还是他们只是表达愤怒的方式不同？

sentences.en: I'm actually kind of interested as to whether or not Chip and I will have the same answer.
sentences.zh: 我其实挺好奇我和奇普的回答会不会一样。

sentences.en: I'll start if I can, Chip, and then we'll see what you say.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话我先来，奇普，然后我们看看你会说什么。

sentences.en: My answer is no.
sentences.zh: 我的回答是不会。

sentences.en: My answer is that the triggers that set us off the perceived unfairness and the reactions are pretty much the same.
sentences.zh: 我的回答是，引发我们生气的触发因素——那些被认为不公平的事以及我们的反应——基本上都是一样的。

sentences.en: Some early studies showed that women would cry more when they were angry and men would not cry more.
sentences.zh: 一些早期研究表明，女性在生气时会哭得更多，而男性则不会哭得那么多。

sentences.en: Some studies that I've read would say that women are more likely to talk it out rather than men.
sentences.zh: 我读过的一些研究表明，相比男性，女性更有可能通过沟通来解决问题。

sentences.en: But, you know, when I look at the database, I think men and women are pretty much equal in anger.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，当我查看数据库时，我认为男女在愤怒程度上基本上是不相上下的。

sentences.en: Now, not in aggression, of course, because men have larger muscles, larger body mass, and can be more aggressive and do more damage.
sentences.zh: 当然，在攻击性方面则不同，因为男性的肌肉更发达、体重大得多，因此可以更具攻击性并造成更多的破坏。

sentences.en: But with regard to anger, I think the answer is pretty much it's an equal opportunity emotion.
sentences.zh: 不过关于愤怒，我认为答案基本上是它是一种不分对象的平等情绪。

sentences.en: What's your answer, Chip?
sentences.zh: 你的答案是什么，奇普？

sentences.en: I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 我不太确定。

sentences.en: I've come to the same conclusion.
sentences.zh: 我得出了同样的结论。

sentences.en: And I want to go back to one of the first treatment studies that Howie and I did.
sentences.zh: 我想回顾一下我和霍伊做过的最早的治疗研究之一。

sentences.en: And this was in the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 那是在20世纪90年代。

sentences.en: And we were quite naive then.
sentences.zh: 我们当时还挺天真的。

sentences.en: And we really thought anger was a male problem.
sentences.zh: 我们真以为愤怒是男性的问题。

sentences.en: And so we kind of put up advertisements for men who were between the ages of 25 and 50.
sentences.zh: 所以我们登出了广告，面向25到50岁之间的男性。

sentences.en: And the ads went something like this.
sentences.zh: 广告内容大致是这样的。

sentences.en: Are you a man between 25 and 50 and you struggle, you know, controlling your anger?
sentences.zh: 你是一个25到50岁、正努力控制愤怒的男性吗？

sentences.en: And if so, please give our clinic a call.
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，请给我们的诊所打个电话。

sentences.en: We'd like to talk with you and offer you a free treatment for your anger.
sentences.zh: 我们想和你聊聊，并为你提供免费的愤怒治疗。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so we would get calls.
sentences.zh: 于是我们会接到电话。

sentences.en: And back then we had an answering machine, right?
sentences.zh: 那时候我们有一个答录机，对吧？

sentences.en: So we'd go to the clinic and play the calls from the answering machine.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会去诊所播放答录机里的留言。

sentences.en: And I'll never forget that we got a couple calls that sounded like this.
sentences.zh: 我永远不会忘记，我们接到过几个听起来像这样的电话。

sentences.en: You know, I saw your ad and I have an anger problem and I'd like free treatment, but I'm a woman and you people are sexiSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我看到了你们的广告，我确实有愤怒问题，我也想要免费治疗，但我是个女人，你们这些人太性别歧视了。

sentences.en: And after getting a handful of calls like that, we started to wonder, maybe these women are right, you know?
sentences.zh: 在接到好几个这样的电话后，我们开始琢磨，也许这些女人是对的，对吧？

sentences.en: And so I very much agree with the idea that in all sorts of different clinical settings, you'll see anger as a problem for both men and women.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常赞同这种观点，在各种不同的临床环境中，你会发现无论男女，愤怒都是一个问题。

sentences.en: And it's definitely a mistake to assume that women don't suffer from anger probleMs.
sentences.zh: 认为女性不会遭受愤怒问题困扰绝对是个错误。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk for a minute about adaptive and maladaptive anger.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们花一分钟聊聊适应性和非适应性愤怒。

sentences.en: The question is, is anger always bad for you?
sentences.zh: 问题是，愤怒对你来说总是坏事吗？

sentences.en: Well, the answer to that is no.
sentences.zh: 答案是，不。

sentences.en: There is both adaptive and maladaptive anger.
sentences.zh: 愤怒既有适应性的，也有非适应性的。

sentences.en: I go back to the point of anger, when it's adaptive, is a signal.
sentences.zh: 我回到愤怒的意义上，当它是适应性的时候，它是一个信号。

sentences.en: It's not of extreme intensity or duration, but it's a signal that something is going wrong.
sentences.zh: 它没有极端的强度或持续时间，但它是一个信号，表明有什么事情出错了。

sentences.en: When you feel angry inside, you want to say, what's going on in my life?
sentences.zh: 当你内心感到愤怒时，你会想说，我的生活发生了什么？

sentences.en: What's going on with my child?
sentences.zh: 我的孩子怎么了？

sentences.en: Is it important to express the anger at this point?
sentences.zh: 在这个时候表达愤怒重要吗？

sentences.en: Take the example for a moment of your parent with a young child.
sentences.zh: 以带幼童的父母为例。

sentences.en: Let's say the child is three or four years old.
sentences.zh: 比方说孩子三四岁。

sentences.en: The child can walk and it's an inner city child.
sentences.zh: 孩子会走路了，而且是个内城区的孩子。

sentences.en: And the child runs into the street and barely misses being hit by a bus.
sentences.zh: 孩子冲向马路，差一点被公共汽车撞到。

sentences.en: Is that a time to say, oh, honey, please don't do that.
sentences.zh: 那是该说，哦，亲爱的，请别那样做的时候吗？

sentences.en: Or is that a time to kind of be a little aroused and agitated and say to the child, never do that again.
sentences.zh: 还是该有点情绪激动、有点焦躁，对孩子说，永远不要那样做。

sentences.en: In that kind of situation, you want what we call one trial learning.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，你会希望实现我们所说的一次尝试学习。

sentences.en: You can't expect to take 10 or 15 trials of the child running into the street before you try to control his or her behavior.
sentences.zh: 你不能指望让孩子在马路上试个10次或15次，再去尝试控制他或她的行为。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So in that sense, the anger for the parent is a signal to take an effective action.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上讲，父母的愤怒是一个采取有效行动的信号。

sentences.en: Let's talk for a minute about people in relationships where the level of anger and anger tolerance is really different.
sentences.zh: 我们花一分钟聊聊身处亲密关系中的人们，他们的愤怒水平和愤怒容忍度截然不同。

sentences.en: So say one partner grew up in a household with a great deal of anger expression, while the other came from a background where anger wasn't acceptable,
sentences.zh: 比如一个伴侣在一个充斥着大量愤怒表达的家庭中长大，而另一个则来自一个愤怒不可接受的背景，

sentences.en: just wasn't expressed or rarely expressed.
sentences.zh: 也就是根本不表达或者很少表达。

sentences.en: Can such a couple reach some kind of a detente that works for both of them?
sentences.zh: 这样的伴侣能达成某种对双方都有效的缓和状态吗？

sentences.en: And if so, how?
sentences.zh: 如果能，怎么达成？

sentences.en: Well, it's kind of interesting because I think in all relationships, there has to be some kind of detente about lots of things, not only anger,
sentences.zh: 这挺有意思的，因为我认为在所有的关系中，对很多事情都必须有某种缓和状态，不仅仅是愤怒，

sentences.en: but about how you spend your money and what kind of religion do you want to bring a child up in?
sentences.zh: 还包括你们怎么花钱，以及你想让孩子信仰什么宗教？

sentences.en: And or how often do you want to go on vacation?
sentences.zh: 或者你们多久想去度一次假？

sentences.en: And no man and woman, let's say, or no two partners who get together are going to be the same on any of these levels, including anger.
sentences.zh: 比方说，没有哪个男人和女人，或者说没有哪两个在一起的伴侣能在所有这些层面上完全一致，愤怒也一样。

sentences.en: So for me, and again, I'm interested in Chip's reaction.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说——再次声明，我对奇普的反应很感兴趣。

sentences.en: For me, the most important part of making your relationship work is what we call assertiveness training.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，让你们的关系运转起来最重要的一部分就是我们所说的自我主张训练。

sentences.en: And by that, I mean not the common definition, but assertiveness really means the proper and appropriate expression of emotion and desire for change.
sentences.zh: 我的意思不是通常的定义，自我主张实际上意味着恰当且合适地表达情绪和改变的愿望。

sentences.en: So those couples that you mentioned, the both partners have to say things like, take an example,
sentences.zh: 所以你提到的那些伴侣，双方都必须说类似这样的话，举个例子，

sentences.en: when you spend so much of your money on clothing and I observe that I feel kind of annoyed, not angry, bitter, hostile, rageful, but I feel annoyed.
sentences.zh: 当你把这么多钱花在买衣服上时，我发现自己感到有点烦恼——不是愤怒、痛苦、敌意、暴怒，而是我感到烦恼。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I'd like to talk to you about that, because my sense is I'd like to spend more of our money on vacations and you'd seem to want to spend more of it on clothing.
sentences.zh: 我想和你聊聊这个，因为我的感觉是我想把更多的钱花在度假上，而你似乎想把更多的钱花在衣服上。

sentences.en: Let's talk about this and get it onto the table.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈这个，把它摆到明面上来。

sentences.en: So open discussion, starting off with the feeling.
sentences.zh: 所以要公开讨论，从感受开始。

sentences.en: I feel annoyed.
sentences.zh: 我觉得烦恼。

sentences.en: I feel mildly angry.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有点生气。

sentences.en: I feel somewhat agitated.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有点焦虑。

sentences.en: Let's talk about it.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈吧。

sentences.en: That's the way to get through this.
sentences.zh: 这是度过难关的方法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But not accusatory.
sentences.zh: 但不要指责。

sentences.en: Not accusatory.
sentences.zh: 不要指责。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: As a matter of fact, I'm happy you say that, Kim, because accusatory verbalizations are unfortunately a major part of anger.
sentences.zh: 事实上，很高兴你这么说，金，因为指责性的言辞不幸的是愤怒的主要组成部分。

sentences.en: Think of it in terms of child rearing.
sentences.zh: 从抚养孩子的角度来想想。

sentences.en: You know, you make me so angry, saying to your daughter or son, you cause so much problems, so many problems for me.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你让我太生气了，对你的女儿或儿子说，你给我惹了这么多麻烦，这么多的麻烦。

sentences.en: So, yeah, you don't want any of that blame.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，你不需要任何这种指责。

sentences.en: You know, it's an interesting question, Kim.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一个有趣的问题，金。

sentences.en: I'm kind of smirking here on the side,
sentences.zh: 我在这里有点暗自得意，

sentences.en: because I don't recall ever seeing a study that looked at different kinds of couples and their anger patterns and looking at potential compatibility.
sentences.zh: 因为我不记得曾见过有研究探讨过不同类型的伴侣及其愤怒模式，并考察潜在的相容性。

sentences.en: And so, there's a lot of unanswered questions in the anger arena.
sentences.zh: 所以，在愤怒领域还有很多未解的问题。

sentences.en: I would just say that we tend to grow through relationships and having close relationships with others helps us question our own patterns.
sentences.zh: 我只想说，我们往往通过关系成长，与他人建立亲密关系有助于我们审视自己的模式。

sentences.en: But the example you brought up raises all sorts of questions.
sentences.zh: 但你提出的例子引发了各种各样的问题。

sentences.en: So, at the extreme ends, you have people that are kind of avoidant and anything that's uncomfortable, they won't discuss or talk about.
sentences.zh: 因此，在极端情况下，有些人有些回避倾向，任何让人不舒服的事情他们都不讨论或谈论。

sentences.en: And on the other extreme, you have people that engage in intimidating and threatening behaviors that shut others down.
sentences.zh: 而在另一个极端，有些人会采取恐吓和威胁的行为，让其他人闭嘴。

sentences.en: And so, I'd have to imagine that if you have a couple where partners are on the extreme ends of both of those, on different ends of the extremes on both of those dimensions,
sentences.zh: 所以，我不得不设想，如果你有一对伴侣，双方都处于这两者的极端，处于这两个维度极端的不同端，

sentences.en: that it's probably not going to go very well.
sentences.zh: 那可能不会有什么好结果。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk about the idea of catharsis, so that some people feel that when you're angry or even just stressed, that the best thing to do is scream and yell and let it out.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们来聊聊宣泄的概念，有些人觉得当你生气甚至只是压力大时，最好的做法就是大喊大叫、发泄出来。

sentences.en: In the past few years, we've seen rage rooms, for example, where people pay money to go into a room and scream and smash things.
sentences.zh: 在过去几年里，我们看到了诸如发泄屋之类的东西，人们花钱进到一个房间里尖叫并砸碎东西。

sentences.en: Dr. DeFrede, let me ask you, what do you think of this idea?
sentences.zh: 德弗雷德博士，请教您一下，您怎么看这个想法？

sentences.en: Do rage rooms and primal screams help people deal effectively with anger and frustration, or is this counterproductive?
sentences.zh: 发泄屋和原始呐喊能帮助人们有效应对愤怒和挫折吗，还是说这适得其反？

sentences.en: In terms of people who struggle with anger difficulties, it's counterproductive.
sentences.zh: 就那些与愤怒困难作斗争的人而言，这适得其反。

sentences.en: And this kind of worries me because the treatment landscape right now seems a little bit like the Wild WeSt.
sentences.zh: 这让我有点担忧，因为现在的治疗领域看起来有点像狂野西部。

sentences.en: And what I mean by that is you have all sorts of different practitioners.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你有各种各样不同的从业者。

sentences.en: You have folks that are licensed and credentialed.
sentences.zh: 你有获得执照和资格认证的人。

sentences.en: You have what I would describe as life coaches who offer their opinions.
sentences.zh: 你有我所描述的、发表意见的生活教练。

sentences.en: And then you have other people that are kind of advice givers and let's call them influencers.
sentences.zh: 然后你还有其他一些给出建议的人，我们称他们为网红。

sentences.en: And there's lots of mythology and misinformation out there.
sentences.zh: 外面有很多神话和错误信息。

sentences.en: And catharsis is one of those.
sentences.zh: 宣泄就是其中之一。

sentences.en: And I saw this on my local news channel the other day.
sentences.zh: 前几天我在本地新闻频道上看到了这个。

sentences.en: They were talking about primal scream.
sentences.zh: 他们在谈论原始呐喊。

sentences.en: And I was really kind of shocked.
sentences.zh: 我当时真的有点震惊。

sentences.en: But this is a problematic intervention.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个有问题的干预手段。

sentences.en: And so, you can think of anyone who suffers from emotional excess.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以想想任何受情绪过剩困扰的人。

sentences.en: So, let's say depression or anxiety.
sentences.zh: 比方说抑郁或焦虑。

sentences.en: You would never turn to someone who's suffering from depression and say, hey, you know, if you don't have the energy to go to work today and you're not feeling confident,
sentences.zh: 你绝不会对一个遭受抑郁折磨的人说，嘿，你知道的，如果你今天没有精力去上班，而且感觉没有自信，

sentences.en: just go back to bed.
sentences.zh: 那就回床上躺着吧。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: You wouldn't take someone who's anxious and say, you know, when you're at the cocktail party and you feel a little bit activated,
sentences.zh: 你不会对一个焦虑的人说，你知道的，当你在鸡尾酒会上感到有点被激活时，

sentences.en: just walk out of the room and leave the party and avoid it.
sentences.zh: 直接走出房间离开派对，逃避它吧。

sentences.en: And so, that's kind of what catharsis is.
sentences.zh: 所以，宣泄差不多就是这样。

sentences.en: We're telling people when you're angry, go with the action tendency that's built into the emotion.
sentences.zh: 我们在告诉人们，当你生气时，顺应内嵌在情绪中的行动倾向。

sentences.en: And really, the trick is to sort of do the opposite of that, is to fight against the action tendency and to kind of ask yourself the question, you know,
sentences.zh: 而实际上，诀窍在于做相反的事情，去对抗这种行动倾向，并问自己一个问题，

sentences.en: where's my anger taking me in this moment?
sentences.zh: 此时此刻我的愤怒把我带向了何方？

sentences.en: And can you try some different behaviors?
sentences.zh: 你能尝试一些不同的行为吗？

sentences.en: And so, when people are anxious, we ask them not to avoid.
sentences.zh: 因此，当人们焦虑时，我们要求他们不要逃避。

sentences.en: When people are depressed, we ask them to push themselves against that feeling of, you know, pulling back from their lives.
sentences.zh: 当人们抑郁时，我们要求他们克制那种想要从生活中抽离出来的感觉。

sentences.en: And when people are angry, we ask them to not give in to the urge to yell and scream and vent and punch and hit things.
sentences.zh: 当人们生气时，我们要求他们不要屈服于大喊大叫、尖叫、发泄、出拳和殴打物体的冲动。

sentences.en: And so, there's been a number of studies on this.
sentences.zh: 所以，对此已经有很多研究了。

sentences.en: There's been studies in the 70s, 80s, 90s, and a couple in the 2000s.
sentences.zh: 70年代、80年代、90年代都有过研究，2000年代也有几项。

sentences.en: Almost no one in the academic arena is studying this anymore because we know the answer.
sentences.zh: 学术界几乎没有人再研究这个了，因为我们已经知道答案了。

sentences.en: This is actually an intervention that makes people worse because what you're practicing is connecting the internal emotion of anger with problematic verbal behaviors or aggressive behaviors.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是一种让情况变得更糟的干预手段，因为你所练习的是将内在的愤怒情绪与有问题的言语行为或攻击行为联系起来。

sentences.en: It's interesting because the section of APA's website that offers information for controlling anger before it controls you is consistently one of the most accessed areas of the entire site.
sentences.zh: 很有意思的是，美国心理学会官网上提供关于“在愤怒控制你之前控制愤怒”信息的板块，一直是整个网站访问量最高的区域之一。

sentences.en: And what that says to me is that people are having anger problems and they don't know where to go to get the help.
sentences.zh: 这对我说明的是，人们正面临愤怒问题，但他们不知道该去哪里寻求帮助。

sentences.en: Do you think as a society that we're giving people the information and the tools that they need to understand and control their anger?
sentences.zh: 你认为作为社会，我们是否在向人们提供理解和控制愤怒所需的信息和工具？

sentences.en: Well, of course, I can put in a plug for the American Psychological Association because podcasts like this and some of the other informational resources that you have
sentences.zh: 当然，我可以为美国心理学会打个广告，因为像这样的播客以及你们拥有的其他一些信息资源

sentences.en: really does help the public really does help the public.
sentences.zh: 确实对公众有帮助，确实对公众有帮助。

sentences.en: We do try to get scientific information out to the public.
sentences.zh: 我们确实在努力向公众普及科学信息。

sentences.en: And this notion of catharsis is like one of the most important areas because it's shocking to me that after all of these years, the question still comes up.
sentences.zh: 而这个宣泄的概念是最重要的领域之一，因为令我震惊的是，历经这么多年，这个问题仍然会被提出来。

sentences.en: And as Chip said, we know the answer.
sentences.zh: 正如奇普所说，我们知道答案。

sentences.en: If you practice being angry, you will become more effective at being angry.
sentences.zh: 如果你练习生气，你就会变得更擅长生气。

sentences.en: There's no such thing as letting it out.
sentences.zh: 根本没有“发泄出来”这回事。

sentences.en: And by the way, I would just use that term.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我只想用这个词。

sentences.en: It's not like you have two quarts of anger inside of you and you're going to let it out like like the historic notion of bloodletting will let it out.
sentences.zh: 这不像是你体内有两夸脱的愤怒，你要像历史上放血的概念那样把它放出来。

sentences.en: You know what it is, is behavioral practice.
sentences.zh: 你知道这是什么吗，这是行为练习。

sentences.en: And if you practice yelling and screaming and throwing and hitting and breaking, you're going to become more effective at yelling and screaming and hitting and breaking, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 如果你练习大喊大叫、尖叫、乱扔、殴打和砸碎，你就会变得更擅长尖叫、大喊、殴打、砸碎等等。

sentences.en: So if I have an anger management issue and I go to see a psychologist or another licensed practitioner who's going to help me, what can I expect?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我有愤怒管理问题，我去咨询心理学家或其他能帮我的有执照的从业者，我能期待什么？

sentences.en: What will that person tell me I should be doing to get control of my life and my anger?
sentences.zh: 那个人会告诉我应该做些什么来掌控我的生活和愤怒吗？

sentences.en: It really depends on the practitioner and how they were trained.
sentences.zh: 这确实取决于从业者以及他们接受过什么培训。

sentences.en: And so we have to have a little truth in advertising here that we don't know as much about anger as we do anxiety and depression.
sentences.zh: 所以我们得在此坦诚相告，我们对愤怒的了解不如对焦虑和抑郁的了解那么多。

sentences.en: And so there's a lot of variability, I think, in how treatment is delivered.
sentences.zh: 因此我认为在治疗的实施方式上存在很大差异。

sentences.en: I think both of us can speak to what some of the best practices might look like.
sentences.zh: 我们俩都可以谈谈最佳实践大概是什么样子的。

sentences.en: And one of the first steps is to understand what anger looks like in the context of the person's life.
sentences.zh: 第一步是了解愤怒在个人生活背景下的表现。

sentences.en: And so not everyone's anger patterns are the same.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是每个人的愤怒模式都一样。

sentences.en: People cause damage to different parts of their lives, their relationships, their work lives.
sentences.zh: 人们对他们生活的不同部分造成了破坏，他们的关系，他们的工作生活。

sentences.en: Some people have trouble with impulsiveness and aggression.
sentences.zh: 有些人存在冲动和攻击性问题。

sentences.en: And so it's not a cookie cutter approach.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是一种千篇一律的方法。

sentences.en: And so we like to start off by analyzing our clients' individual episodes of anger and understand the components that make up those anger episodes.
sentences.zh: 因此我们喜欢从分析客户的个别愤怒发作事件开始，了解构成这些愤怒事件的各个组成部分。

sentences.en: And once we understand that, it becomes a little bit more obvious to the client and to us what areas we might look at in terms of intervention.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们理解了这一点，对于客户和我们来说，我们在干预方面可以关注哪些领域就会变得更加明显。

sentences.en: You know, it's interesting you asked that question, Kim.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你问这个问题很有意思，金。

sentences.en: And I want to come back to you for a moment.
sentences.zh: 我想再回到你刚才的话题。

sentences.en: Look at the questions that you're asking.
sentences.zh: 看看你问的这些问题。

sentences.en: They are mostly what I'm going to call social interpersonal.
sentences.zh: 它们大多是我所称的社会人际方面的。

sentences.en: And when Chip says we don't know as much about anger and we have to therefore be careful and do a good interview and tailor our treatment, consider this.
sentences.zh: 当奇普说我们对愤怒了解不够，因此必须小心谨慎、做好访谈并定制治疗方案时，想想这一点。

sentences.en: One of the outcomes of anger that we haven't spoken about is bad decision making.
sentences.zh: 我们尚未讨论过的一个愤怒的后果就是糟糕的决策。

sentences.en: When you're angry, that may not be the time to ask your boss for a raise.
sentences.zh: 当你感到生气时，也许并不是向老板要求加薪的好时机。

sentences.en: We haven't spoken about that.
sentences.zh: 我们还没有谈过那个。

sentences.en: We haven't spoken about the fact that there are lots of biophysical medical outcomes of sustained anger.
sentences.zh: 我们还没有谈过这样一个事实：持续的愤怒会带来很多生物物理和医学上的不良后果。

sentences.en: Sustained anger over the years is associated with high blood pressure, digestive problems, heart disease, stroke.
sentences.zh: 多年来持续的愤怒与高血压、消化问题、心脏病和中风有关。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So as clinicians, we also want to look into those factors, into the cognitive factors.
sentences.zh: 因此，作为临床医生，我们也希望深入研究这些因素，即认知因素。

sentences.en: We haven't spoken too much.
sentences.zh: 我们谈得还不够多。

sentences.en: And I must say Chip is an expert in this area in terms of the effects of anger on arrest and incarceration and the criminal justice system.
sentences.zh: 而且我必须说，查普在这个领域是专家，特别是在愤怒对逮捕、监禁以及刑事司法系统的影响方面。

sentences.en: I mean, it's such a broad negative emotion when it becomes extreme that we really have a lot more to learn.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当它变得极端时，这是一种非常强烈的负面情绪，我们确实还有很多东西需要了解。

sentences.en: And I think also in terms of what we're seeing in society at large, I mean, it seems like there's almost a kind of virality.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，从我们在整个社会中看到的情况来看，我的意思是，似乎几乎有一种病毒式传播的现象。

sentences.en: Is that the right word?
sentences.zh: 这是个合适的词吗？

sentences.en: Where my being angry can trigger other people to be angry.
sentences.zh: 即我的愤怒会引发其他人发怒。

sentences.en: I'm thinking, for example, of the Ahmaud Arbery case that was just tried in Georgia, where, you know, these neighbors all got together and fed off of each other.
sentences.zh: 比如，我想到刚刚在佐治亚州审判的阿莫德·阿伯里案，你知道，这些邻居聚在一起，情绪互相煽动。

sentences.en: I mean, is that a typical thing where people who are angry feed other angry people?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个典型现象吗？愤怒的人会去煽动其他愤怒的人？

sentences.en: You know, there's a wonderful word that I learned a few years ago called emnification.
sentences.zh: 你知道，几年前我学到一个非常棒的词，叫做“敌对化”。

sentences.en: E-M-E-M.
sentences.zh: E-M-E-M.

sentences.en: Emnification.
sentences.zh: 敌对化。

sentences.en: It means finding an enemy.
sentences.zh: 意思是寻找一个敌人。

sentences.en: And yeah, you may live in a community where one person is targeted as an enemy,
sentences.zh: 是的，你可能生活在这样一个社区里：某个人被当作敌人锁定，

sentences.en: and then you wind up gossiping about that person and generating the anger against that person by talking about it constantly, by not giving that person,
sentences.zh: 然后你最终会八卦那个人，通过不断谈论来煽动针对那个人的愤怒，不给那个人，

sentences.en: whether it's a minority man running down the street or whatever it is, not giving that person the benefit of the doubt, but saying, we've known all along about that person.
sentences.zh: 无论是一个在街上奔跑的少数族裔男子还是别的什么人，不给那个人合理的信任，而是说：我们一直都看透那个人了。

sentences.en: You know about that person, Kim.
sentences.zh: 你了解那个人的，金。

sentences.en: You know about that person, Chip.
sentences.zh: 你了解那个人的，查普。

sentences.en: I know about that person.
sentences.zh: 我知道那个人是什么样。

sentences.en: And yes, we do feed on each other and make it worse.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们的确会互相煽动，让情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: And there's also this proliferation of reality television shows in American culture.
sentences.zh: 在美国文化中，真人秀电视节目也大量激增。

sentences.en: And it seems like people that are selected to be on reality shows often have poor emotion regulation, which can be entertaining to watch, right?
sentences.zh: 而且似乎被选中参加真人秀的人往往情绪调节能力较差，看他们发脾气可能会很有趣，对吧？

sentences.en: But unfortunately,
sentences.zh: 但遗憾的是，

sentences.en: the types of nasty and verbal rants and sometimes the physically aggressive behaviors that you see on these shows get modeled as legitimate ways to resolve disagreements in the face of life's challenges.
sentences.zh: 你在这些节目中看到的那些恶毒的言语爆发，有时甚至是身体攻击行为，被当作面对生活挑战时解决分歧的合乎情理的方式来进行模仿。

sentences.en: So I think that in some cases, we've seen individuals who express their anger in destructive ways receive positive attention, maybe celebrity or some type of financial gain.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，在某些情况下，我们看到那些以破坏性方式表达愤怒的个人获得了积极的关注，也许是名气或某种经济利益。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, these types of reactions in the real world tend to damage relationships and lead to suffering and losses for most people.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，在现实世界中，这类反应往往会破坏关系，并给大多数人带来痛苦和损失。

sentences.en: Do you see cultural differences in anger?
sentences.zh: 你看到愤怒中存在的文化差异了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it always feels to me like, you know, we're a particularly expressive society in that respect.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我总觉得在这方面我们是一个表现欲特别强的社会。

sentences.en: And I know it feels to me like there are other cultures where it's actually verboten.
sentences.zh: 而且我感觉在其他文化中，这是实际上被禁止的。

sentences.en: I'm just wondering if you see that in your research.
sentences.zh: 我只是想知道你在研究中是否观察到了这一点。

sentences.en: Well, you know, cultures are so broad.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，文化太广泛了。

sentences.en: There are so many different types of cultures.
sentences.zh: 有太多不同类型的文化。

sentences.en: If you go to Nepal, if you go to India, where Chip and I have both been, if you look at some of those cultures where they the Janes,
sentences.zh: 如果你去尼泊尔，如果你去印度——查普和我都去过——如果你看看其中一些文化，比如耆那教徒，

sentences.en: they don't even want you to step on an ant on the floor because that would be a sign of aggression.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至不希望你在地板上踩死一只蚂蚁，因为那会是侵略性的标志。

sentences.en: Then you look at some of the southern United States subcultures where there is this culture of of getting even, of being macho, of taking the bull by the horns,
sentences.zh: 然后你看看美国南方的某些亚文化，那里存在着一种以牙还牙、崇尚硬汉、迎难而上的文化，

sentences.en: no matter what the outcome.
sentences.zh: 不管结果如何。

sentences.en: The culture is so broad that I don't think I could make a firm statement about it.
sentences.zh: 文化太广泛了，我觉得我无法对此做出明确的断言。

sentences.en: Chip, any thoughts on your end?
sentences.zh: 查普，你有什么想法吗？

sentences.en: You know, it's it's a it's a great yeah, I mean, I can share personal stories from my travels of how anger sort of looks differently in different cultures.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一个……这是一个……非常好……是的，我的意思是，我可以分享我旅行中的个人故事，关于愤怒在不同文化中看起来如何不同。

sentences.en: But I think what's important to remember is that anger as a basic emotion does exist across all cultures.
sentences.zh: 但我认为重要的是要记住，愤怒作为一种基本情绪确实存在于所有文化中。

sentences.en: So whether you live in the most remote rainforest in the world or the most cosmopolitan city, you have you know, you're wired to experience anger.
sentences.zh: 所以无论你住在世界上最偏远的雨林还是最国际化的城市，你都知道，你的大脑天生就会体验愤怒。

sentences.en: What changes drastically across cultures are the expressive patterns that are sort of permitted within that culture.
sentences.zh: 在不同文化中发生急剧变化的是该文化中所允许的表达模式。

sentences.en: And so you see more expressive cultures and cultures that are less expressive.
sentences.zh: 因此你会看到有些文化表现力更强，有些文化表现力较弱。

sentences.en: I found in my travels that when you go to countries where expressing anger is is not considered appropriate, people are still angry and you sit down and have lunch with them.
sentences.zh: 我在旅行中发现，当你去到那些表达愤怒被认为是不合适的国家时，人们仍然会生气，你会和他们坐下来一起吃午饭。

sentences.en: And, you know, they're kind of gossiping negatively and sort of, you know, kind of undermining some of their enemies and colleagues.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们会在私底下消极地八卦，你知道的，有点贬低他们的敌人和同事。

sentences.en: They're not they're not looking angry, but they're doing it in different ways.
sentences.zh: 他们看起来并没有生气，但他们是在用不同的方式这样做。

sentences.en: And so I think anger is always there.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为愤怒一直都在。

sentences.en: It's just what what are the rules of the culture that permit anger or sort of dampen certain expressive patterns down?
sentences.zh: 只是文化的规则是什么，允许愤怒还是压制某些表达模式？

sentences.en: Yeah, I would say, Chip, not only the rules of the culture, but maybe the rules of the individual.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想说，查普，不仅是文化的规则，也许还有个人的规则。

sentences.en: And by that, I mean, I've been to Russia quite a few times, as has Chip.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我去过俄罗斯很多次，查普也是。

sentences.en: And I think back in the late 1990s, I did a large scale study of anger and what we call our anger model, meaning look at the various components of anger.
sentences.zh: 我想在20世纪90年代末，我做过一项大规模的愤怒研究，研究我们所谓的愤怒模型，也就是审视愤怒的各个组成部分。

sentences.en: And basically, I found no differences.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我没有发现任何差异。

sentences.en: The Russians responded to our anger model, which was basically the triggers of anger, what have you what you thought about the trigger, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人对我们的愤怒模型的反应是完全一样的，这个模型基本上包括愤怒的诱因、你对诱因的看法等等。

sentences.en: Russians and Americans responded exactly the same way.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人和美国人的反应完全相同。

sentences.en: Yet, as we make this broadcast today, Putin is invading Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 然而，在我们今天进行这场广播时，普京正在入侵乌克兰。

sentences.en: So and he's acting, I believe, as a dictator, meaning as a as a single single minded person.
sentences.zh: 所以他正在行动，我认为他就像一个独裁者，也就是一个专断独行的人。

sentences.en: So when we talk about anger and aggression, I think there may be broad cultural differences.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们谈论愤怒和攻击性时，我认为可能存在广泛的文化差异。

sentences.en: But there are also an awful lot of individual differences.
sentences.zh: 但同时也存在着非常多的个体差异。

sentences.en: So one of the things that we like to do when we're talking about these kinds of issues for our listeners is to try to give them some effective strategies if they're struggling with with the question at hand.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们为听众讨论这类问题时，我们喜欢做的事情之一，就是尽量为他们提供一些有效的策略，如果他们正在与手头的问题作斗争的话。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, I know you've both written a book about this.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，我知道你们俩都写过关于这方面的书。

sentences.en: What are the highlights of what you found around the most effective strategies that people can use to manage their own anger?
sentences.zh: 关于人们用来管理自己愤怒的最有效策略，你们发现的核心要点是什么？

sentences.en: People who don't necessarily need to go for a clinical intervention, but are trying to work through things themselves.
sentences.zh: 那些不一定需要接受临床干预，但正试图自己解决问题的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, we may have different answers on this one.
sentences.zh: 是的，在这个问题上我们可能会有不同的答案。

sentences.en: I think for me, one of them is to ask yourself, is this issue all that important?
sentences.zh: 我想对我来说，其中一点就是问问自己：这个问题真的那么重要吗？

sentences.en: If my child was not selected for the school play, if the other worker at work did get a better desk, if any of those things occurred, is this really such a big deal?
sentences.zh: 如果我的孩子没有被选上参加学校话剧，如果单位里的另一个同事确实分到了更好的办公桌，如果诸如此类的事情发生了，这真的是一件大事吗？

sentences.en: Is it such an awful and terrible and horrible thing?
sentences.zh: 这是一件如此可怕、糟糕和糟糕透顶的事情吗？

sentences.en: We have lots of examples we could give where the child who's not selected for the school play, who's treated unfairly, goes on to be a great actor, right?
sentences.zh: 我们可以举出很多例子：那些没有被选上参加学校话剧、受到不公正对待的孩子，后来成了一名伟大的演员，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it's motivating.
sentences.zh: 因为这具有激励作用。

sentences.en: So we don't really know the answer to what various life events we'll have on our future.
sentences.zh: 所以我们其实并不知道各种生活事件会对我们的未来产生什么影响。

sentences.en: And if there's a simple thing, I would say is, think about whether it's worthwhile making a mountain out of a molehill in the issue that's affecting you right now.
sentences.zh: 如果有一个简单的方法，我会说：想一想，把你现在面临的问题小题大做是否真的值得。

sentences.en: Kim, I think there's reason for optimism.
sentences.zh: 金，我认为有理由保持乐观。

sentences.en: That there's been a handful of sort of meta-analytic reviews in the treatment area, and they all point to the same conclusion.
sentences.zh: 在治疗领域有过少数的元分析评论，它们都指向同一个结论。

sentences.en: That people that get treatment do better than people that don't.
sentences.zh: 接受治疗的人比不接受治疗的人表现得更好。

sentences.en: There is a little less clarity around what are the best interventions for anger.
sentences.zh: 对于什么是针对愤怒的最佳干预措施，目前还不是那么明确。

sentences.en: We don't have as much research to sort of point to, is there a treatment of choice?
sentences.zh: 我们没有足够的研究来指出是否存在一种首选疗法。

sentences.en: And so that question gets asked a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以这个问题经常被问到。

sentences.en: What should I be doing to manage my anger?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么做来控制我的愤怒？

sentences.en: The bad news is we don't have a treatment of choice.
sentences.zh: 坏消息是我们没有首选疗法。

sentences.en: The good news is we don't have a treatment of choice.
sentences.zh: 好消息是我们没有首选疗法。

sentences.en: And there's a number of things that practitioners and individuals can do to combat their own sort of anger patterns and still be evidence-based.
sentences.zh: 从业人员和个人可以做很多事情来对抗他们自身的愤怒模式，同时仍然保持循证依据。

sentences.en: And so we kind of liken, in our approach at least, we liken it to a menu-driven approach.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的方法，至少在我们的方法中，我们将其比作菜单驱动的方法。

sentences.en: It's kind of like going to a restaurant and selecting those interventions that seem to fit best with the context of your life and the kinds of anger problems that you're having.
sentences.zh: 这有点像去餐馆点菜，选择那些最适合你生活背景以及你所遇到的愤怒问题的干预措施。

sentences.en: And I can read to you some of those from the list, but this could be a very long conversation.
sentences.zh: 我可以向你宣读清单中的一些内容，但这可能会是一场非常漫长的对话。

sentences.en: But I think there's things like managing your lifestyle, getting enough sleep, eating, you know, watching your eating habits.
sentences.zh: 但我认为有一些事情，比如管理你的生活方式、保证充足的睡眠、注意饮食习惯。

sentences.en: We teach people that they don't have to confront everything.
sentences.zh: 我们教导人们，他们不必对每件事都进行对抗。

sentences.en: Agree to let go of some things.
sentences.zh: 学会放下一些事情。

sentences.en: You don't have to confront, you know, you don't have to be the policeman of the universe and, you know, scream and yell out your window when someone cuts you off.
sentences.zh: 你不必去对抗，你知道，你不必成为宇宙警察，当有人插队时在窗户大喊大叫。

sentences.en: So learning to sidestep provocations.
sentences.zh: 所以要学会避开挑衅。

sentences.en: Instead of reacting on autopilot, try to come up with some innovative ways to respond to some of the challenges in your life.
sentences.zh: 与其按自动驾驶模式反应，不如想出一些创新的方式来应对生活中的某些挑战。

sentences.en: There's a whole bunch of interventions around relaxation, mindfulness, meditation that get people to calm their body, to slow down their impulsive decision-making.
sentences.zh: 有一大堆围绕放松、正念、冥想的干预措施，可以让人们平静身体，放慢冲动的决策速度。

sentences.en: One of my favorites is exposure, the kind of way you think about exposure interventions for anxiety,
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的方法之一是暴露疗法，就像你对焦虑症的暴露干预措施的理解一样，

sentences.en: where we actually practice with people dealing with some of the challenging scenarios in their lives and have them come up with better behaviors.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上与人们一起练习应对他们生活中一些具有挑战性的情境，让他们想出更好的行为方式。

sentences.en: Then there's a whole bunch of interventions in the thinking area,
sentences.zh: 然后，在思维领域还有一大堆干预措施，

sentences.en: helping people kind of look at their thoughts in the moment when they're angry and try to be more realistic and less distorted.
sentences.zh: 帮助人们在生气的那一刻审视自己的想法，尽量更加现实，减少扭曲。

sentences.en: Then we have this idea of just kind of going through life with a more flexible philosophy.
sentences.zh: 然后我们有这样一种理念，即带着更加灵活的人生哲学去生活。

sentences.en: There's also some good information bubbling up around teaching people to approach life with a little bit more forgiveness and compassion.
sentences.zh: 围绕着教导人们以更多的宽容和同情心来对待生活，也有一些很好的信息正在涌现。

sentences.en: And then we have a whole area of just teaching people skills for how they sort of negotiate outcomes with people, how we mentioned assertiveness training.
sentences.zh: 然后我们还有一个完整的领域，就是教导人们如何与他人协商结果的技能，正如我们提到的果断训练。

sentences.en: But sometimes we'll teach people just basic interpersonal skills like what are you doing with your hands when you're talking to people and disagreeing with them?
sentences.zh: 但有时我们会教给人们一些基本的人际交往技能，比如当你与人交谈并与他们意见不合时，你的手在做什么？

sentences.en: How loud is your tone of voice?
sentences.zh: 你的语调有多大？

sentences.en: How close do you get to them?
sentences.zh: 你离他们有多近？

sentences.en: And so sometimes our clients can benefit from some really basic coaching in their skills.
sentences.zh: 所以有时我们的客户可以从一些非常基础的技能辅导中受益。

sentences.en: And so there's not one intervention.
sentences.zh: 因此，并没有某一种单一的干预措施。

sentences.en: There's a whole host of things here.
sentences.zh: 这里有一大堆各种各样的方法。

sentences.en: And, Howie, I don't know how you'd answer that question about what the best treatment is for people that have anger probleMs.
sentences.zh: 霍伊，我不知道你对“针对有愤怒问题的人最好的治疗方法是什么”这个问题会作何回答。

sentences.en: You know, I think Kim's question was, could I come up with, like, one thing to say?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想金的问题是，我能不能想出一个可以说的点？

sentences.en: And that's why I went to the don't make a mountain out of a molehill.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我选择了“不要小题大做”。

sentences.en: But I think everything that you say is absolutely correct, Chip, and on the money, and I'm totally with you.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你所说的一切绝对都是正确的，查普，切中要害，我完全同意你的看法。

sentences.en: So I would now come back and say, one of the things that I think people can do is read self-help books.
sentences.zh: 所以我要回过头来说，我认为人们可以做的事情之一就是阅读自助书籍。

sentences.en: Because what Chip has just gone through is our series of interventions, which basically include worksheets, explanations, opportunities for practice.
sentences.zh: 因为查普刚才讲的是我们的一系列干预措施，基本上包括工作表、解释、练习机会。

sentences.en: So, yes, all of the data show that going to a mental health professional like a psychologist trained in the area of anger does work, will be helpful.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，所有数据都表明，去看心理健康专业人士，比如在愤怒领域接受过培训的心理学家，确实有效，会有所帮助。

sentences.en: Those are the meta-analyses.
sentences.zh: 这些就是元分析的结果。

sentences.en: But reading some good self-help books can also be helpful.
sentences.zh: 但阅读一些好的自助书籍也会有所帮助。

sentences.en: Now, I want to say something I think is important here.
sentences.zh: 现在，我想说一件我认为很重要的事。

sentences.en: There are a lot of not good self-help books out there.
sentences.zh: 市面上有许多并不好的自助书籍。

sentences.en: Books that are telling you that you have a volcano inside of you that's erupting, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，有些书告诉你，你的体内有一座正在喷发的火山。

sentences.en: I think, Chip, and I do not believe you have a volcano inside of you.
sentences.zh: 我想，查普和我都不相信你的体内有一座火山。

sentences.en: I think the only thing you have inside of you is your heart and your liver and your pancreas and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 我认为你体内唯一的东两就是你的心脏、肝脏、胰腺以及所有诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: So what you really want is books.
sentences.zh: 所以你真正需要的是书籍。

sentences.en: And there are a few of them out there, ours, but some others, by people who've been studying anger for all of their lives.
sentences.zh: 市面上有一些这样的书，包括我们写的，还有一些其他人写的，这些人一生都在研究愤怒。

sentences.en: I mean, Chip and I have been doing this, I have to say, since the early 1990s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不得不说，查普和我从20世纪90年代初就开始做这件事了。

sentences.en: And we do have maybe, I'm going to say,
sentences.zh: 我们大概有，我要说的是，

sentences.en: 10 other professionals around the United States who've also been in the anger area and have been studying it as their life mission since the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 美国还有其他10名专业人士，他们也涉足愤怒领域，自20世纪90年代以来一直将其作为一生的使命进行研究。

sentences.en: And they've put out a series of self-help books, as we have, that can be very effective.
sentences.zh: 他们和我们一样，出版了一系列非常有效的自助书籍。

sentences.en: But be careful about the ones that are talking about intervolcanoes or making false promises.
sentences.zh: 但要注意那些谈论内心火山或做出虚假承诺的书籍。

sentences.en: Those are the ones you're going to be careful of.
sentences.zh: 那些是你要小心的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think our advice is to seek out credentialed, licensed practitioners that have some experience in the area,
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为我们的建议是寻找有资质、有执照且在该领域有一些经验的从业人员，

sentences.en: whether you're talking about consuming self-help materials or going to see a professional in the context of a therapeutic treatment.
sentences.zh: 无论你是讨论获取自助材料，还是在治疗环境中去看专业人士。

sentences.en: What I've noticed over the last five or 10 years with the increase in social media is mental health professionals giving a list of what they consider themselves to be expert in.
sentences.zh: 我注意到在过去五到十年里，随着社交媒体的增加，心理健康专业人士列出了一份他们认为自己是专家的领域清单。

sentences.en: And they list maybe 20 different areas, anxiety and depression and anorexia nervosa and marital problems and geriatric and what have you.
sentences.zh: 他们列出了大概20个不同的领域，焦虑、抑郁、神经性厌食症、婚姻问题、老年病学等等。

sentences.en: Chip and I don't say that, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想查普和我并没有这么说。

sentences.en: Chip and I say anger has been our life passion.
sentences.zh: 查普和我可以说，愤怒是我们一生的热情所在。

sentences.en: And there are, as I said, there are 10 or 15 other people that really have made that anger their life passion.
sentences.zh: 而且正如我所说，还有其他10到15个人真正将愤怒作为他们一生的热情所在。

sentences.en: Those are the ones that I would be trying to consult with and to read their books.
sentences.zh: 这些人是我会尽量去咨询并阅读其书籍的人。

sentences.en: Well, thank you.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你们。

sentences.en: I think that's been very helpful advice.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是非常有用的建议。

sentences.en: And I hope our listeners appreciate that.
sentences.zh: 我希望我们的听众能对此深表感激。

sentences.en: We'll try to have some resources on our web page for people to refer to.
sentences.zh: 我们会在网页上提供一些资源供人们参考。

sentences.en: So I appreciate your joining me today.
sentences.zh: 所以我很感激你们今天加入我的节目。

sentences.en: Dr. Tafrady, Dr. Casanoff, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 塔弗迪博士，卡萨诺夫博士，非常感谢你们。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 我的荣幸。

sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org 或在 Apple、Stitcher 或你获取播客的任何地方找到往期的《心理学面面观》节目。
